**English draft for R5 review.**

If you think someone tricked you or your family into giving money, **tell a grown-up right away**. Don't hide it!

There's a special helpline number in India for this: **1930**. A grown-up can call it and also tell the bank.

Being tricked is **not your fault**. Tricksters are clever. Telling quickly is the brave and smart thing to do.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

Is it your fault if a trickster fools you?
questions.explanation: Anyone can be tricked. Speaking up is what matters.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

The first hours after a fraud matter most. Money moved through UPI or cards can often be **frozen** if reported before it is withdrawn or moved again (the "golden hour").

**Step 1: Contain.** Call the bank's official number to block cards, UPI and net banking; change passwords and sign out of other devices.
**Step 2: Report.** Call **1930** (national cyber-crime helpline) and file at **cybercrime.gov.in**. Note the acknowledgement number.
**Step 3: Preserve evidence.** Keep transaction IDs, UTR numbers, times, screenshots, phone numbers and links; don't delete the chat.
**Step 4: Follow up.** Submit a written complaint to the bank. Under RBI rules on limiting customer liability, reporting unauthorised electronic transactions quickly (within three working days) can limit what you lose. Escalate to the bank's grievance officer, and then to the RBI Ombudsman if unresolved.

Shame keeps many victims silent, which helps scammers repeat the trick. Reporting protects others and builds the data used to block fraud numbers.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.
